question.text: Per recent SEBI circular referenced in the chapter, a Category III AIF is NOT permitted to adopt which of the following models?

answer.text: Charging differential management fees across classes
Issuing different classes of units to institutional vs retail investors
A 'priority distribution model' where one class of investors receives higher share of profits at the cost of another class
Disclosing separate Series NAV for each class

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'As per recent SEBI Circular, no Category III AIF can adopt such a priority distribution model, in which one class of investors are getting a higher share of profits, at the cost of another class of investors.' The Trap: Differential management fees, multi-class units, separate Series NAV are all PERMITTED - only priority (junior/senior waterfall) distribution is banned. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-E flag this ban. Cross-exam: XIX-D (Cat I/II) has its own priority-distribution constraints. Manager's Pro-Tip: Audit existing PPMs against the priority-distribution ban - some pre-2022 structures inadvertently baked in senior/junior economics through 'preferred' return tranches. Amend and get investor consent before next close.
